# Overview

This single document reproduces **every number and figure** reported in the paper
from the raw cascade tables in `data/`. Knit it (RStudio → *Knit*, or
`rmarkdown::render("marine_hazard_chains_reproduction.Rmd")`) to regenerate:

```{r paths}
## Relative paths from the repository root (cross-platform via file.path()).
data_dir   <- "data"
marine_f   <- file.path(data_dir, "marine", "tsunami_Dohmen_2025_EQ.docx")
inland_f   <- file.path(data_dir, "mainland_china",
                        paste0("earthquake_table_China_4_", c("E", "N", "SW", "NW"), ".docx"))
## landslide cause and entry status of the 58 marine events, copied from the catalogue of
## Dohmen et al. (2025; PANGAEA, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.979839), see data/README.md
catalogue_f <- file.path(data_dir, "marine", "marine_events_catalogue_status.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(marine_f), all(file.exists(inland_f)), file.exists(catalogue_f))

## Inland comparison network (paper Methods, Data and encoding): an inland earthquake has its epicentre on
## land and a hazard chain that does not involve a tsunami. Ten events of the China tables
## (nine Taiwan events and the 1994 Taiwan Strait event) have offshore epicentres or
## near-coast cascades and are excluded, which leaves 84 events and 500 chains.
inland_excluded <- c("1910-0023-TWN", "1922-0014-TWN", "1951-0044-TWN", "1959-0050-TWN",
                     "1986-0133-TWN", "1994-0307-CHN", "2002-0172-TWN", "2006-0688-TWN",
                     "2018-0059-TWN", "2024-0189-TWN")
```

# Helper functions

`read_doc()` reads the first table of a `.docx`; the only column used is the
machine-readable **`Proposed Encoding`** field (chains such as
`SEQ,TS;TS,CFL;CFL,PP;`). `build_graph()` turns those encodings into a directed
graph: chains are split on `;`, pairs on `,`, whitespace is trimmed so `" TS"`
and `"TS"` are not treated as different nodes, and the union of all chains is
de-duplicated. **Self-loops are retained** here (one edge, `PP -> PP`, exists in
the record and is part of the 152-edge fine network; it is removed only for the
15-class comparison, exactly as the paper states). `event_of()` assigns every row
to its source event (the ID is carried forward over continuation rows), so that
`build_graph(..., exclude = )` can drop whole events.

```{r helpers}
read_doc <- function(path) {
  tb <- docxtractr::docx_extract_tbl(docxtractr::read_docx(path), tbl_number = 1)
  as.data.frame(tb, check.names = FALSE)
}

## robustly locate the "Proposed Encoding" column (dot or space in the name)
encoding_of <- function(df) df[[ grep("Encoding", names(df), ignore.case = TRUE)[1] ]]

## source event of every row: the ID is carried forward over continuation rows, which
## have an empty ID, a bare direction (east, south, west, north, centre) or start with "and "
event_of <- function(df) {
  id <- trimws(as.character(df[[1]])); cur <- NA_character_; ev <- character(length(id))
  for (k in seq_along(id)) {
    if (!is.na(id[k]) && nzchar(id[k]) &&
        !grepl("^[\u4e1c\u5357\u897f\u5317\u4e2d]$", id[k]) && !startsWith(id[k], "and ")) cur <- id[k]
    ev[k] <- cur }
  ev
}

## exclude: event IDs whose rows are dropped (an event matches if its ID starts with one of them)
build_graph <- function(paths, exclude = NULL) {
  x   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(paths, read_doc))
  enc <- encoding_of(x)
  if (length(exclude)) {
    ev  <- event_of(x)
    enc <- enc[!vapply(ev, function(e) !is.na(e) && any(startsWith(e, exclude)), logical(1))]
  }
  from <- character(0); to <- character(0)
  for (s in enc) for (seg in strsplit(s, ";")[[1]]) {
    pr <- trimws(strsplit(seg, ",")[[1]])
    if (length(pr) >= 2 && all(nzchar(pr[1:2]))) { from <- c(from, pr[1]); to <- c(to, pr[2]) }
  }
  final <- dplyr::distinct(data.frame(from = from, to = to))  # unique directed edges (self-loops kept)
  igraph::graph_from_data_frame(final, directed = TRUE)
}
```

# Marine network {#marine-network}

The fine marine network is built from `r basename(marine_f)` (366 documented
cascade chains, 39 peril codes).

```{r marine-network}
g_marine <- build_graph(marine_f)
cat(sprintf("Marine fine network: %d nodes, %d directed edges (incl. 1 self-loop PP->PP)\n",
            vcount(g_marine), ecount(g_marine)))
```

# Table 1: node degrees {#table-1-node-degrees}

In/out degree of every node on the **fine** network (self-loop retained, so the
PP self-loop contributes +1 to both PP's in- and out-degree, giving PP = in 9 /
out 1, as in the paper). `net = out − in`.

```{r table-2}
deg_tab <- data.frame(
  Code = V(g_marine)$name,
  In   = degree(g_marine, mode = "in"),
  Out  = degree(g_marine, mode = "out"),
  Net  = degree(g_marine, mode = "out") - degree(g_marine, mode = "in"),
  row.names = NULL)
## the paper's Table 1 lists nodes with in- or out-degree >= 7 (upper quartile)
core <- deg_tab[deg_tab$In >= 7 | deg_tab$Out >= 7, ]
knitr::kable(core[order(-core$Out, -core$In), ], row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 1 — core nodes (in- or out-degree >= 7).")
```

# Table 2: four-layer net flow {#table-2-four-layer-net-flow}

Nodes are aggregated into the four cascade layers; **net flow = out − in** summed
over each layer's members. Expected: **+42 / +1 / −16 / −27** (sums to 0).

```{r table-3}
layer_fine <- c(
  SEQ="Trigger", EQ="Trigger", AS="Trigger", VE="Trigger",
  SLS="Natural", CLS="Natural", LS="Natural", RO="Natural", LB="Natural", SA="Natural",
  LI="Natural", GU="Natural", SUB="Natural", MB="Natural", TS="Natural", CFL="Natural",
  FF="Natural", MED="Natural", WP="Natural", WD="Natural", DI="Natural", FA="Natural",
  PHF="Engineering", SDF="Engineering", SPF="Engineering", SCF="Engineering", NFA="Engineering",
  FI="Engineering", EX="Engineering", CF="Engineering", NF="Engineering",
  MTD="Consequence", BI="Consequence", EC="Consequence", PP="Consequence",
  HD="Consequence", IR="Consequence", SU="Consequence", CP="Consequence")
L4 <- c("Trigger", "Natural", "Engineering", "Consequence")

layer_flow <- function(g, lmap, levels) {
  lay <- factor(lmap[V(g)$name], levels = levels)
  o <- tapply(degree(g, mode = "out"), lay, sum); o[is.na(o)] <- 0
  i <- tapply(degree(g, mode = "in"),  lay, sum); i[is.na(i)] <- 0
  data.frame(Layer = levels, Nodes = as.integer(table(lay)[levels]),
             `Out-flow` = as.integer(o[levels]), `In-flow` = as.integer(i[levels]),
             `Net flow` = as.integer(o[levels] - i[levels]),
             `Net %`   = round((o[levels] - i[levels]) / ecount(g) * 100, 1),
             check.names = FALSE)
}
t3 <- layer_flow(g_marine, layer_fine, L4)
knitr::kable(rbind(t3, data.frame(Layer="Total", Nodes=sum(t3$Nodes),
             `Out-flow`=sum(t3$`Out-flow`), `In-flow`=sum(t3$`In-flow`),
             `Net flow`=sum(t3$`Net flow`), `Net %`=round(sum(t3$`Net %`),1), check.names=FALSE)),
             row.names = FALSE, caption = "Table 2 — four-layer net flow (fine network).")
```

# Table 3: 15-class comparison {#table-3-15-class-comparison}

Both chains are reduced to the **same 15 classes** and **simplified (duplicate
edges and self-loops removed)** before any metric is computed. The 39 → 15
mapping (the paper's Table 8, in the Methods) is:

```{r coarse-map}
coarse_map <- c(
  SEQ="EQ or AS", AS="EQ or AS", EQ="EQ or AS", VE="EQ or AS",
  GU="Mass Slide", SLS="Mass Slide", CLS="Mass Slide", LI="Mass Slide", MB="Mass Slide",
  SUB="Mass Slide", LS="Mass Slide", RO="Mass Slide", LB="Mass Slide", SA="Mass Slide",
  PHF="Critical Infra. Fail.", SDF="Critical Infra. Fail.", CF="Critical Infra. Fail.",
  NFA="Critical Infra. Fail.", SPF="Critical Infra. Fail.",
  BI="Business Interr.", MTD="Business Interr.", WP="Water Dil.", WD="Water Dil.",
  NF="Critical NET Fail.", SCF="Critical NET Fail.", FA="Flora an Fauna", MED="Flora an Fauna",
  FI="Fire", EX="Fire", IR="Healthcare Deg.", HD="Healthcare Deg.",
  TS="Flood", CFL="Flood", FF="Flood",
  EC="Econ. Crisis", DI="Disease", PP="Phy.-Psych. Trauma", CP="Culture Perils", SU="Social Unrest")
stopifnot(length(setdiff(V(g_marine)$name, names(coarse_map))) == 0)  # every marine node is mapped
```

```{r build-coarse}
## contract the fine marine graph to 15 classes; the inland tables are already 15-class
grp <- factor(coarse_map[V(g_marine)$name])
g_marine_c <- contract(g_marine, as.integer(grp), vertex.attr.comb = "first")
V(g_marine_c)$name <- levels(grp)
g_marine_c   <- simplify(g_marine_c, remove.multiple = TRUE, remove.loops = TRUE)  # -> 57 edges

g_inland   <- build_graph(inland_f, exclude = inland_excluded)
g_inland_c <- simplify(g_inland, remove.multiple = TRUE, remove.loops = TRUE)  # -> 14 classes, 44 edges

## size of the inland record before and after the exclusion
xin <- do.call(rbind, lapply(inland_f, read_doc)); ev_in <- event_of(xin)
has_chain <- !is.na(encoding_of(xin)) & nzchar(trimws(encoding_of(xin)))
is_excl   <- vapply(ev_in, function(e) !is.na(e) && any(startsWith(e, inland_excluded)), logical(1))
cat(sprintf("China tables: %d events, %d chains | inland network: %d events, %d chains, %d classes, %d edges (%d events excluded)\n",
            length(unique(ev_in[has_chain])), sum(has_chain),
            length(unique(ev_in[has_chain & !is_excl])), sum(has_chain & !is_excl),
            vcount(g_inland_c), ecount(g_inland_c), length(unique(ev_in[has_chain & is_excl]))))
```

The full Table 3 — comparable topology metrics **and** the four-layer net flow,
combined in one table (Marine vs Inland), exactly as in the paper. Disease
does not occur in the inland record, so the inland network has 14 classes.
**Out/in-degree centralisation uses the paper's Eq. (4)**,
`sum(d_max − d_i) / (N−1)^2` (identical to `igraph::centr_degree` once self-loops
are removed).

```{r table-4}
## out/in-degree centralisation, paper Eq. (4): sum(d_max - d_i) / (N-1)^2
Cfree <- function(g, mode) { d <- degree(g, mode = mode); N <- vcount(g)
  sum(max(d) - d) / ((N - 1)^2) }

## 15-class -> four-layer map, for the net-flow rows
layer15 <- c("EQ or AS"="Trigger",
  "Mass Slide"="Natural","Water Dil."="Natural","Flora an Fauna"="Natural","Flood"="Natural","Disease"="Natural",
  "Critical Infra. Fail."="Engineering","Critical NET Fail."="Engineering","Fire"="Engineering",
  "Business Interr."="Consequence","Healthcare Deg."="Consequence","Econ. Crisis"="Consequence",
  "Phy.-Psych. Trauma"="Consequence","Culture Perils"="Consequence","Social Unrest"="Consequence")

## every reported Table 3 value for one 15-class graph, as a labelled character column
table4_col <- function(g) {
  nf <- layer_flow(g, layer15, L4)$`Net %`          # Trigger / Natural / Engineering / Consequence
  c(`Nodes / edges`             = sprintf("%d / %d", vcount(g), ecount(g)),
    `Network density`           = sprintf("%.3f", edge_density(g, loops = FALSE)),
    `Out-degree centralisation` = sprintf("%.3f", Cfree(g, "out")),
    `In-degree centralisation`  = sprintf("%.3f", Cfree(g, "in")),
    `Max out-degree`            = sprintf("%d",   max(degree(g, mode = "out"))),
    `Pure sources / sinks`      = sprintf("%d / %d", sum(degree(g, mode="in")==0),
                                                     sum(degree(g, mode="out")==0)),
    `Mean path length`          = sprintf("%.2f", mean_distance(g, directed = TRUE)),
    `Net flow — Trigger`        = sprintf("%+.1f%%", nf[1]),
    `Net flow — Natural`        = sprintf("%+.1f%%", nf[2]),
    `Net flow — Engineering`    = sprintf("%+.1f%%", nf[3]),
    `Net flow — Consequence`    = sprintf("%+.1f%%", nf[4]))
}
marine_col   <- table4_col(g_marine_c)
inland_col <- table4_col(g_inland_c)
knitr::kable(data.frame(Metric = names(marine_col),
                        `Marine (15 classes)` = unname(marine_col),
                        `Inland`              = unname(inland_col),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 3 — 15-class comparison: topology metrics and four-layer net flow.")
```

# Methods, Data and encoding: composition of the two records {#record-composition}

**What it shows / why:** the numbers that the Data and encoding subsection of the Methods gives for the two records. For
the marine record: the 58 source events, their time span and how they split over
time, and how the catalogue of Dohmen et al. (2025) attributes the 57 events taken
from it. Their landslide cause and entry status are copied from the catalogue
(PANGAEA, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.979839) into
`data/marine/marine_events_catalogue_status.csv`. Nine events are attributed to a
cause other than an earthquake or flagged as erroneous entries. The chunk lists them,
counts their chains and checks that excluding them leaves the sources, hubs and layer
ordering reported in the Results and the marine column of Table 3 unchanged. For the inland
record: the span of the 84 inland events.

```{r record-composition}
## directed pairs of a set of encodings, parsed exactly as in build_graph()
rc_pairs <- function(enc) {
  out <- list()
  for (s in enc) for (seg in strsplit(s, ";")[[1]]) {
    pr <- trimws(strsplit(seg, ",")[[1]])
    if (length(pr) >= 2 && all(nzchar(pr[1:2]))) out[[length(out) + 1]] <- pr[1:2] }
  if (length(out)) do.call(rbind, out) else matrix(character(0), 0, 2)
}

## marine record: source event of every chain, and the year in the event ID
xm      <- read_doc(marine_f)
rc_ev   <- event_of(xm)
rc_enc  <- encoding_of(xm)
rc_has  <- !is.na(rc_enc) & nzchar(trimws(rc_enc))
rc_evs  <- unique(rc_ev[rc_has])
rc_year <- as.integer(sub(".*_(\\d{3,4})$", "\\1", rc_evs))
stopifnot(length(rc_evs) == 58, sum(rc_has) == 366, !anyNA(rc_year))
cat(sprintf("marine record: %d events, %d chains, AD %d-%d | before 1900: %d, 1900-1999: %d, since 2000: %d\n",
            length(rc_evs), sum(rc_has), min(rc_year), max(rc_year),
            sum(rc_year < 1900), sum(rc_year >= 1900 & rc_year <= 1999), sum(rc_year >= 2000)))

## catalogue attribution (cause: EQ earthquake, U unknown, V volcanic activity,
## A anthropogenic activity, PA paraglacial conditions, PR precipitation)
cat_tab <- read.csv(catalogue_f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
stopifnot(setequal(cat_tab$event_id, rc_evs))
in_cat  <- !is.na(cat_tab$landslide_cause)
cause_n <- table(cat_tab$landslide_cause[in_cat])
cat(sprintf("in the catalogue: %d events (not listed: %s) | cause: %s | erroneous entries: %d\n",
            sum(in_cat), paste(cat_tab$event_id[!in_cat], collapse = ", "),
            paste(names(cause_n), cause_n, collapse = ", "),
            sum(grepl("erroneous", cat_tab$catalogue_status))))

## the nine events: a cause other than an earthquake, or an erroneous entry
noneq_events <- cat_tab$event_id[in_cat & (cat_tab$landslide_cause != "EQ" |
                                            grepl("erroneous", cat_tab$catalogue_status))]
## build_graph(exclude =) matches IDs by prefix, so make sure it hits exactly these events
stopifnot(sum(vapply(rc_evs, function(e) any(startsWith(e, noneq_events)), logical(1))) == length(noneq_events))
nine_tab <- cat_tab[cat_tab$event_id %in% noneq_events, c("event_id", "landslide_cause", "catalogue_status")]
nine_tab$chains <- vapply(nine_tab$event_id, function(e) sum(rc_has & rc_ev == e), integer(1))
knitr::kable(nine_tab, row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Event", "Cause", "Catalogue status", "Chains"),
             caption = sprintf("The %d catalogue events attributed to a cause other than an earthquake or flagged as erroneous (%d of the %d chains).",
                               nrow(nine_tab), sum(nine_tab$chains), sum(rc_has)))

## what excluding them changes
g_rc <- build_graph(marine_f, exclude = noneq_events)
ekey <- function(g) with(igraph::as_data_frame(g), paste(from, to, sep = "->"))
cat(sprintf("couplings documented only by these events: %s | network without them: %d nodes, %d edges\n",
            paste(setdiff(ekey(g_marine), ekey(g_rc)), collapse = ", "), vcount(g_rc), ecount(g_rc)))
rc_summary <- function(g) {
  din <- degree(g, mode = "in"); dout <- degree(g, mode = "out")
  nf  <- layer_flow(g, layer_fine, L4)$`Net flow`
  c(`Pure sources`                     = paste(sort(names(din)[din == 0]), collapse = ", "),
    `Top out-degree / top in-degree`   = sprintf("%s (%d) / %s (%d)", names(which.max(dout)), max(dout),
                                                 names(which.max(din)), max(din)),
    `NF in / out`                      = sprintf("%d / %d", din[["NF"]], dout[["NF"]]),
    `Layer net flow T/N/E/C`           = paste(sprintf("%+d", nf), collapse = " / "),
    `Net flow decreases down the layers` = as.character(all(diff(nf) < 0)))
}
grp_rc <- factor(coarse_map[V(g_rc)$name])
g_rc_c <- contract(g_rc, as.integer(grp_rc), vertex.attr.comb = "first")
V(g_rc_c)$name <- levels(grp_rc)
g_rc_c <- simplify(g_rc_c, remove.multiple = TRUE, remove.loops = TRUE)
rc_cmp <- data.frame(Quantity           = c(names(rc_summary(g_marine)), paste("Table 3:", names(marine_col))),
                     `All 58 events`    = c(rc_summary(g_marine), marine_col),
                     `Without the nine` = c(rc_summary(g_rc), table4_col(g_rc_c)), check.names = FALSE)
rc_cmp$Unchanged <- rc_cmp[[2]] == rc_cmp[[3]]
knitr::kable(rc_cmp, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Sources, hubs and layer ordering of the fine network, and the marine column of Table 3, with and without the nine events.")

## inland record: the span of the 84 inland events (year = first four digits in the event ID)
rc_in_evs  <- unique(ev_in[has_chain & !is_excl])
rc_in_year <- as.integer(regmatches(rc_in_evs, regexpr("[0-9]{4}", rc_in_evs)))
stopifnot(length(rc_in_evs) == 84, length(rc_in_year) == 84)
cat(sprintf("inland record: %d events, %d-%d\n", length(rc_in_evs), min(rc_in_year), max(rc_in_year)))
```

# Table 6 / Results, Node removal {#node-removal}

**What it shows / how it is made:** the cascade reach $R(G)$ is the number of
ordered hazard pairs $(i, j)$, $i \neq j$, joined by a directed path (the PP
self-loop is ignored). Removing a set $S$ deletes its nodes together with their
edges. Pairs that start or end in $S$ would vanish under any removal, so the
paper's Eq. (6) compares the reduced graph with the full graph restricted to the
same nodes,
$\Delta R(S) = \bigl(R_{V\setminus S}(G) - R(G-S)\bigr) / R_{V\setminus S}(G)$,
the share of the remaining connectivity that depends on paths through $S$. The
best sets of one, two and three nodes are found by **exhaustive search** over the
nine engineering nodes (main result) and, for reference, over all 27
process-layer nodes. This reproduces Table 6 and the 619 / 576 / 409 pair counts
of the Node removal subsection.

```{r node-removal}
gr <- simplify(g_marine, remove.loops = TRUE, remove.multiple = TRUE)  # reachability ignores the self-loop
reach_mat <- function(g) { D <- distances(g, mode = "out"); is.finite(D) & D > 0 }
M0 <- reach_mat(gr); dimnames(M0) <- list(V(gr)$name, V(gr)$name)   # M0[i, j]: j reachable from i in G
R0 <- sum(M0)

## Eq. (6): base = R_{V\S}(G), after = R(G - S), dR in %
removal <- function(S) {
  keep  <- setdiff(V(gr)$name, S)
  base  <- sum(M0[keep, keep])
  after <- sum(reach_mat(delete_vertices(gr, S)))
  c(base = base, after = after, dR = 100 * (base - after) / base)
}
## exhaustive search: the `top` best sets of size k from a candidate pool
best_sets <- function(pool, k, top = 2) {
  cmb <- combn(pool, k, simplify = FALSE)
  r   <- vapply(cmb, function(S) removal(S)[["dR"]], numeric(1))
  o   <- order(-r)[seq_len(min(top, length(r)))]
  data.frame(Size = k, `Removed set` = vapply(cmb[o], paste, character(1), collapse = " + "),
             Reduction = sprintf("%.1f%%", r[o]), check.names = FALSE)
}
eng  <- names(layer_fine)[layer_fine == "Engineering"]                 # 9 nodes
proc <- names(layer_fine)[layer_fine %in% c("Natural", "Engineering")]  # 27 nodes
## list each pool by single-node leverage, so that sets are printed strongest node first
by_single <- function(pool) pool[order(-vapply(pool, function(v) removal(v)[["dR"]], numeric(1)))]
eng <- by_single(eng); proc <- by_single(proc)
cf <- removal("CF")
cat(sprintf("R(G) = %d ordered pairs | removing CF: %d -> %d pairs among the remaining nodes (%.1f%%)\n",
            R0, cf[["base"]], cf[["after"]], cf[["dR"]]))

single <- data.frame(Node = eng, r = vapply(eng, function(v) removal(v)[["dR"]], numeric(1)))
single <- single[order(-single$r), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(Node = single$Node, Reduction = sprintf("%.1f%%", single$r)), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 6 (engineering candidates) — single nodes.")
knitr::kable(rbind(best_sets(eng, 2), best_sets(eng, 3)), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 6 (engineering candidates) — best and next-best pairs and triples (exhaustive search over 9 nodes).")
nat <- names(layer_fine)[layer_fine == "Natural"]
nat_r <- vapply(nat, function(v) removal(v)[["dR"]], numeric(1))
cat(sprintf("best natural-process node: %s (%.1f%%)\n", names(which.max(nat_r)), max(nat_r)))
knitr::kable(rbind(best_sets(proc, 1), best_sets(proc, 2), best_sets(proc, 3)), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Table 6 (process-layer candidates, reference) — best and next-best sets (exhaustive search over 27 nodes).")
cat(sprintf("CF + FI + TS (fire in place of critical network failure): %.1f%%\n", removal(c("CF", "FI", "TS"))[["dR"]]))
```

# Figure 1 {#figure-1}

**What it shows / how it is made:** the fine 39-node marine network, drawn twice
with a shared force-directed layout (`igraph::layout_with_fr`, `set.seed(123)`
for reproducibility). Node **colour and size encode degree** on a yellow→red
scale; panel (a) uses in-degree, panel (b) out-degree (zero-out-degree nodes
white). This is the code behind the paper's `fig01.png`.

```{r figure-1, fig.width=13, fig.height=6.2}
pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#FFF886", "#d21d13"))
plot_deg <- function(g, layout, metric, zero_white = FALSE) {
  m <- metric / max(metric)
  col <- pal(500)[as.numeric(cut(m, breaks = 500))]; if (zero_white) col[metric == 0] <- "white"
  s <- sqrt(metric); vs <- 4 + (if (max(s)==0) 0 else s/max(s)) * 14
  plot(g, layout = layout, vertex.size = vs, vertex.color = col,
       vertex.frame.color = adjustcolor("grey30", .5),
       vertex.label = V(g)$name, vertex.label.family = "sans",
       vertex.label.color = "black", vertex.label.cex = .8, vertex.label.font = 2,
       edge.arrow.size = .35, edge.width = .6, edge.curved = .15,
       edge.color = adjustcolor("grey60", .45))
}
## helper: write a 300-dpi TIFF (LZW) and optionally a PNG of a plot, then draw it inline
export_fig <- function(plotfun, base, w, h) {
  dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
  ## 300-dpi PNG
  png(file.path("figures", paste0(base, "_300dpi.png")),
      width = w, height = h, units = "in", res = 300)
  plotfun(); invisible(dev.off())
  ## 300-dpi TIFF (LZW)
  tiff(file.path("figures", paste0(base, "_300dpi.tif")),
       width = w, height = h, units = "in", res = 300, compression = "lzw")
  plotfun(); invisible(dev.off())
  plotfun()   # inline for the knitted HTML
}
set.seed(123); lay1 <- layout_with_fr(g_marine, niter = 3000)
draw_fig1 <- function() {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
  plot_deg(g_marine, lay1, degree(g_marine, mode = "in"));  title("(a) in-degree")
  plot_deg(g_marine, lay1, degree(g_marine, mode = "out"), zero_white = TRUE); title("(b) out-degree")
}
export_fig(draw_fig1, "fig01", 13, 6.2)
```

# Figure 2 {#figure-2}

**What it shows / how it is made:** the marine (15 classes) and inland (14
classes) networks on **one shared force-directed layout** so each class sits in
the same place across panels. Four panels: marine in/out degree, inland in/out
degree; colour and size encode degree. The layout is computed, as in v1.0.1, on
the marine network together with the complete China tables (all 94 events), so
that every class keeps the position it has in the earlier version of the figure; the
inland panels themselves draw only the 84 inland events. This is the code behind
`fig02_300dpi.png`.

```{r figure-2, fig.width=12, fig.height=11}
abbr <- c("EQ or AS"="EQ","Mass Slide"="MS","Critical Infra. Fail."="CIF","Business Interr."="BI",
  "Water Dil."="WD","Critical NET Fail."="CNF","Flora an Fauna"="FA","Fire"="FI",
  "Healthcare Deg."="HD","Flood"="FL","Econ. Crisis"="EC","Disease"="DI",
  "Phy.-Psych. Trauma"="PP","Culture Perils"="CP","Social Unrest"="SU")
g_china_all_c <- simplify(build_graph(inland_f), remove.multiple = TRUE, remove.loops = TRUE)  # layout only
common <- sort(unique(c(V(g_marine_c)$name, V(g_china_all_c)$name)))
uni <- graph_from_data_frame(
  rbind(igraph::as_data_frame(g_marine_c), igraph::as_data_frame(g_china_all_c)),
  directed = TRUE, vertices = data.frame(name = common))
set.seed(123); lay2 <- layout_with_fr(uni, niter = 3000); rownames(lay2) <- V(uni)$name
panel <- function(g, mode, ttl) {
  m <- degree(g, mode = mode); mm <- if (max(m)==0) m else m/max(m)
  col <- pal(500)[as.numeric(cut(mm, breaks = 500))]; if (mode=="out") col[m==0] <- "white"
  s <- sqrt(m); vs <- 12 + (if (max(s)==0) 0 else s/max(s)) * 26
  plot(g, layout = lay2[V(g)$name, ], vertex.size = vs, vertex.color = col,
       vertex.frame.color = adjustcolor("grey30", .5), vertex.label = abbr[V(g)$name],vertex.label.family = "sans",
       vertex.label.color = "black", vertex.label.cex = 1.4, vertex.label.font = 2,
       edge.color = adjustcolor("grey60", .5), edge.width = .7, edge.arrow.size = .35,
       edge.curved = .15, main = ttl)
}
draw_fig2 <- function() {
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 2.5, 1))
  panel(g_marine_c, "in", "(a) Marine — in-degree");    panel(g_marine_c, "out", "(b) Marine — out-degree")
  panel(g_inland_c, "in", "(c) Inland — in-degree"); panel(g_inland_c, "out", "(d) Inland — out-degree")
}
export_fig(draw_fig2, "fig02", 12, 11)
```

# Figure 3 / Results, Robustness and sampling sufficiency {#figure-3-robustness}

**What it shows / how it is made:** the 366 chains cluster under **58 source
events (tsunamis)**, so all resampling is at the **event level** (cluster
bootstrap). Panel (a) is the edge-accumulation (sampling-sufficiency) curve;
panel (b) is the fraction of `B=1000` event-bootstrap resamples in which each
qualitative conclusion holds (C1 pure sources; C2 dominant hubs SEQ/CF; C3
NF-as-convergence; C4 monotone four-layer cascade). The same `B` resamples
also yield the 95% bootstrap intervals for the two hub degrees quoted in
the Robustness subsection (submarine-earthquake out-degree and critical-infrastructure-failure
in-degree); these are printed below the figure rather than plotted. The first
check of the Robustness subsection --- raising the edge-inclusion threshold to `>=1`, `>=2` and
`>=3` independent events, which progressively removes low-frequency links --- is
also tabulated below the figure, showing which of C1--C4 survive at each
threshold (only C3 fails, at the `>=3` core of 46 edges).

```{r robustness, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.2}
set.seed(1)
x <- read_doc(marine_f)
id <- x[[ grep("^ID$|ID", names(x))[1] ]]; enc <- encoding_of(x)
cur <- NA; ev <- character(length(enc))                     # forward-fill event id
for (i in seq_along(enc)) { if (!is.na(id[i]) && nzchar(trimws(id[i]))) cur <- id[i]; ev[i] <- cur }
chain_edges <- lapply(seq_along(enc), function(i) {
  e <- character(0)
  for (seg in strsplit(enc[i], ";")[[1]]) { pr <- trimws(strsplit(seg, ",")[[1]])
    if (length(pr) >= 2 && all(nzchar(pr[1:2]))) e <- c(e, paste(pr[1], pr[2], sep = "|")) }
  unique(e) })
events   <- unique(ev)
ev_edges <- lapply(events, function(g) unique(unlist(chain_edges[ev == g])))
n_ev <- length(events); full <- length(unique(unlist(ev_edges)))
efreq <- table(unlist(ev_edges))

build_e  <- function(edges) { ee <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(edges, "\\|"))
  graph_from_data_frame(data.frame(from = ee[,1], to = ee[,2]), directed = TRUE) }
concl <- function(g) { dout <- degree(g, mode="out"); din <- degree(g, mode="in")
  nm <- V(g)$name; gv <- function(v,d) if (v%in%nm) d[v] else 0
  L <- layer_fine[nm]; nf <- sapply(L4, function(k) sum(dout[L==k]) - sum(din[L==k]))
  c(C1 = setequal(nm[din==0], c("SEQ","EQ")),
    C2 = (names(which.max(dout))=="SEQ" && names(which.max(din))=="CF"),
    C3 = (gv("NF",din) > gv("NF",dout)),
    C4 = (nf["Trigger"]>nf["Natural"] && nf["Natural"]>nf["Engineering"] &&
          nf["Engineering"]>nf["Consequence"] && nf["Trigger"]>0 && nf["Consequence"]<0)) }

## First check (Results, Robustness and sampling sufficiency): raise the inclusion threshold to >= 1, 2, 3
## independent events. Raising it strips low-frequency (single-event) links;
## C1-C4 are re-tested on each thresholded network to see which conclusions
## survive. (efreq counts, for every directed edge, the number of source
## events in which it appears.)
thr_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(k) {
  keep <- names(efreq)[efreq >= k]
  cn   <- as.logical(concl(build_e(keep)))   # drop internal names; index by position
  data.frame(min_events = k, edges = length(keep),
             C1 = cn[1], C2 = cn[2], C3 = cn[3], C4 = cn[4]) }))

B <- 1000
stab <- rowMeans(sapply(1:B, function(b)
  concl(build_e(unique(unlist(ev_edges[sample(n_ev, n_ev, replace = TRUE)])))))) * 100

## 95% bootstrap intervals for the two hub degrees quoted in the Robustness subsection
## (event-level cluster bootstrap; reported in the text, not plotted in Fig. 3)
deg_boot <- sapply(1:B, function(b) {
  g  <- build_e(unique(unlist(ev_edges[sample(n_ev, n_ev, replace = TRUE)])))
  gd <- function(v, m) { d <- degree(g, mode = m); if (v %in% V(g)$name) d[[v]] else 0L }
  c(SEQ_out = gd("SEQ", "out"), CF_in = gd("CF", "in")) })
deg_ci <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f (95%% CI [%d, %d])", mean(x),
            as.integer(round(quantile(x, .025))), as.integer(round(quantile(x, .975))))

fr  <- seq(.05, 1, .05)
acc <- sapply(fr, function(f) { k <- max(1, round(f*n_ev))
  mean(sapply(1:200, function(s) length(unique(unlist(ev_edges[sample(n_ev, k)]))))) })
## Out-of-sample edge coverage (Results, Robustness and sampling sufficiency), for ALL held-out links and for the
## core links, averaged over many random 5-fold splits. A single split is noisy
## (and R's sample() RNG changed at R 3.6), so we average to get a stable,
## seed-robust value: all links ~74%, core ~96%. The core links are those
## documented in at least two events OF THE HELD-OUT FOLD, so that selecting them
## uses no information from the training events (v1.0.1 counted the events over
## the whole record, which leaks the training events into the selection, ~98%).
R_split  <- 200
fold_cov <- function(fold, core) mean(sapply(1:5, function(f) {
  tr <- unique(unlist(ev_edges[fold != f]))
  te <- unique(unlist(ev_edges[fold == f]))
  if (core) { tef <- table(unlist(ev_edges[fold == f])); te <- names(tef)[tef >= 2] }
  if (length(te) == 0) NA else 100 * sum(te %in% tr) / length(te) }), na.rm = TRUE)
cov_rep  <- sapply(1:R_split, function(r) {
  fold <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = n_ev))
  c(all = fold_cov(fold, FALSE), core = fold_cov(fold, TRUE)) })
all_cov  <- mean(cov_rep["all",  ])
core_cov <- mean(cov_rep["core", ])

draw_fig3 <- function() {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 2.4, 1))
  plot(100*fr, 100*acc/full, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#d21d13", ylim = c(0,100),
       xlab = "Source events (tsunamis) used (%)", ylab = "Unique edges recovered (%)",
       main = "(a) Sampling sufficiency")
  abline(h = core_cov, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
  barplot(stab, col = "#F2A43A", ylim = c(0,100), names.arg = c("C1","C2","C3","C4"),
          ylab = "Holds in resamples (%)", main = "(b) Conclusion stability (event bootstrap)")
  abline(h = 95, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
}
export_fig(draw_fig3, "fig03", 10, 4.2)
cat(sprintf("events=%d | C1..C4 hold in %s%% | out-of-sample coverage: all links %.0f%%, >=2 core %.0f%%\n",
            n_ev, paste(round(stab), collapse="/"), all_cov, core_cov))
cat(sprintf("hub-degree bootstrap (Results, Robustness): SEQ out-degree %s ; CF in-degree %s\n",
            deg_ci(deg_boot["SEQ_out", ]), deg_ci(deg_boot["CF_in", ])))
cat("First check (Results, Robustness) -- which conclusions survive as low-frequency links are removed:\n")
print(thr_check, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Independent-event validation {#independent-event-validation}

**What it shows / why:** three major submarine-earthquake tsunamis that are **not among
the 58 compiled events** — the 2004 Indian Ocean (Sumatra-Andaman), the 1960
Valdivia (Chile) and the 2018 Palu (Sulawesi) events — are encoded as documented,
individually sourced cascade chains in
`data/marine/tsunami_extra_events_2004_1960_2018_EQ.docx` (a `Source` column, ignored
by the analysis, carries the provenance). The 2004 and 1960 events are also absent
from the landslide-tsunami catalogue; the 2018 Palu event is listed in it but was
withheld from the compilation for this test. This section (1) draws the three events
on their own, (2) overlays them on the paper's network, and (3) tests whether the
paper's conclusions survive the new data, with chance baselines for the coverage.

## The three events on their own

```{r extra-network, fig.width=13, fig.height=6.2}
extra_f <- file.path(data_dir, "marine", "tsunami_extra_events_2004_1960_2018_EQ.docx")
g_extra <- build_graph(extra_f)
cat(sprintf("Extra-events network: %d nodes, %d directed edges\n", vcount(g_extra), ecount(g_extra)))
set.seed(123); layE <- layout_with_fr(g_extra, niter = 3000)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
plot_deg(g_extra, layE, degree(g_extra, mode = "in"));  title("(a) in-degree")
plot_deg(g_extra, layE, degree(g_extra, mode = "out"), zero_white = TRUE); title("(b) out-degree")
```

## Old versus new dataset size

```{r dataset-sizes}
noloop <- function(g) ecount(simplify(g, remove.loops = TRUE, remove.multiple = FALSE))
meta <- function(path) {
  x <- read_doc(path); id <- x[[1]]; en <- encoding_of(x)
  cur <- NA; ev <- character(nrow(x)); nch <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(x))) {
    if (!is.na(id[i]) && trimws(id[i]) != "") cur <- trimws(id[i])
    ev[i] <- cur
    if (!is.na(en[i]) && nzchar(trimws(en[i]))) nch <- nch + 1L
  }
  c(events = length(unique(ev)), chains = nch)
}
mo <- meta(marine_f); me <- meta(extra_f)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Dataset = c("Old (tsunami_Dohmen_2025_EQ)", "New (three extra events)"),
  Events  = c(mo[["events"]], me[["events"]]),
  Chains  = c(mo[["chains"]], me[["chains"]]),
  Nodes   = c(vcount(g_marine), vcount(g_extra)),
  `Edges (incl. self-loop)` = c(ecount(g_marine), ecount(g_extra)),
  `Edges (no self-loop)`    = c(noloop(g_marine), noloop(g_extra)),
  check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE, caption = "Node and edge counts of the old and new datasets.")
```

## The three events overlaid on the paper's network

New-event **nodes are coloured by layer** and their **labels are black**. Among the
edges the three events contribute, the **14 links absent from the paper's record are
drawn in dark red**, the remaining new-event edges (already documented) in black, and
every node, edge and label that comes only from the original network in grey. The
dark-red edges are exactly the enrichment the new events add; the black-and-coloured
footprint is what they reconfirm in the paper's structure.

```{r extra-overlay, fig.width=11, fig.height=9.5}
lay_col <- c(Trigger = "#e4572e", Natural = "#2a9d8f",
             Engineering = "#e9a220", Consequence = "#4a6fa5")
E_orig  <- igraph::as_data_frame(g_marine)
E_extra <- igraph::as_data_frame(g_extra)
g_union <- graph_from_data_frame(unique(rbind(E_orig, E_extra)), directed = TRUE)

new_nodes <- V(g_extra)$name
new_ekey  <- paste(E_extra$from, E_extra$to)
ekey_union <- with(igraph::as_data_frame(g_union), paste(from, to))
old_ekey   <- paste(E_orig$from, E_orig$to)
is_new_e   <- ekey_union %in% new_ekey
is_novel_e <- is_new_e & !(ekey_union %in% old_ekey)   # the 14 links absent from the record
is_new_v   <- V(g_union)$name %in% new_nodes

vcol  <- ifelse(is_new_v, lay_col[layer_fine[V(g_union)$name]], "grey88")
vlcol <- ifelse(is_new_v, "black", "grey70")
ecol  <- ifelse(is_novel_e, "#8b0000", ifelse(is_new_e, "black", adjustcolor("grey40", .8)))
ewid  <- ifelse(is_novel_e, 2.4, ifelse(is_new_e, 1.3, .5))

set.seed(123); layU <- layout_with_fr(g_union, niter = 3000)
draw_overlay <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(g_union, layout = layU,
       vertex.size = 7, vertex.color = vcol, vertex.frame.color = adjustcolor("grey40", .5),
       vertex.label = V(g_union)$name, vertex.label.family = "sans",
       vertex.label.color = vlcol, vertex.label.cex = .8, vertex.label.font = 2,
       edge.color = ecol, edge.width = ewid, edge.arrow.size = .3, edge.curved = .12)
  legend("bottomleft", legend = names(lay_col), col = lay_col, pch = 19, bty = "n",
         cex = 1.0, title = "New-event nodes (by layer)")
  legend("bottomright",
         legend = c("novel edge (14; new only)", "new-event edge (also in record)", "original-only edge"),
         col = c("#8b0000", "black", "grey40"), lwd = c(2.4, 1.3, .8), bty = "n", cex = 1.0)
}
## save standalone 300-dpi TIFF + PNG (publication quality), then render inline below
export_fig(draw_overlay, "fig04_overlay_events", 11, 9.5)
```

## Do the conclusions survive the new data?

```{r extra-validation}
selfless <- function(df) df[df$from != df$to, , drop = FALSE]
orig_keys <- with(selfless(igraph::as_data_frame(g_marine)), paste(from, to))

## (A) directed-edge coverage, per event and combined
xx <- read_doc(extra_f); enc <- encoding_of(xx); id <- xx[[1]]
cur <- NA; ev <- character(nrow(xx))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(xx))) { if (!is.na(id[i]) && trimws(id[i]) != "") cur <- trimws(id[i]); ev[i] <- cur }
edges_of <- function(s) {
  e <- c(); for (p in strsplit(s, ";")[[1]]) { pr <- trimws(strsplit(p, ",")[[1]])
    if (length(pr) >= 2 && all(nzchar(pr[1:2])) && pr[1] != pr[2]) e <- c(e, paste(pr[1], pr[2])) }
  unique(e)
}
covA <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(ev), function(g) {
  ek <- unique(unlist(lapply(enc[ev == g], edges_of)))
  data.frame(Event = g, Links = length(ek), `In network` = sum(ek %in% orig_keys),
             Coverage = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(ek %in% orig_keys)), check.names = FALSE) }))
old_ek <- unique(unlist(lapply(enc[ev %in% c("LTT_Chile_1960", "LTT_IndianOcean_2004")], edges_of)))
covA <- rbind(covA, data.frame(Event = "1960 + 2004 (outside the catalogue)", Links = length(old_ek),
              `In network` = sum(old_ek %in% orig_keys),
              Coverage = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(old_ek %in% orig_keys)), check.names = FALSE))
all_ek <- unique(unlist(lapply(enc, edges_of)))
covA <- rbind(covA, data.frame(Event = "ALL THREE", Links = length(all_ek),
              `In network` = sum(all_ek %in% orig_keys),
              Coverage = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(all_ek %in% orig_keys)), check.names = FALSE))
knitr::kable(covA, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("(A) Directed-edge coverage of the three independent events by the paper's network (%d novel enrichment links).",
                               sum(!all_ek %in% orig_keys)))

## the novel couplings, and how many of them involve one of the hubs SEQ, TS, CF or NF
novel_ek <- all_ek[!all_ek %in% orig_keys]
hub_hit  <- vapply(strsplit(novel_ek, " "), function(p) any(p %in% c("SEQ", "TS", "CF", "NF")), logical(1))
cat(sprintf("%d novel couplings: %s\n%d of them involve a hub (SEQ, TS, CF or NF): %s\n",
            length(novel_ek), paste(sub(" ", "->", novel_ek), collapse = ", "),
            sum(hub_hit), paste(sub(" ", "->", novel_ek[hub_hit]), collapse = ", ")))

## (A2) chance baselines for the coverage (Results, Independent-event test): a random network with the same
## nodes and edges, and random rewirings that keep the in- and out-degree of every node
## (edge swaps a->b, c->d  =>  a->d, c->b; Maslov and Sneppen, 2002)
g_s <- simplify(g_marine, remove.loops = TRUE, remove.multiple = TRUE)
n_s <- vcount(g_s)
set.seed(1)
rew_cov <- replicate(1000, {
  g_r <- rewire(g_s, with = keeping_degseq(loops = FALSE, niter = 20 * ecount(g_s)))
  100 * mean(all_ek %in% with(igraph::as_data_frame(g_r), paste(from, to))) })
g_r <- rewire(g_s, with = keeping_degseq(loops = FALSE, niter = 20 * ecount(g_s)))
stopifnot(all(degree(g_r, mode = "in") == degree(g_s, mode = "in")),
          all(degree(g_r, mode = "out") == degree(g_s, mode = "out")))   # degrees are preserved
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Network = c("Random, same nodes and edges (expected)", "Degree-preserving rewiring (1000 networks)",
              "Observed marine network"),
  Coverage = c(sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * ecount(g_s) / (n_s * (n_s - 1))),
               sprintf("mean %.1f%%, 95th percentile %.1f%%, max %.1f%%", mean(rew_cov),
                       quantile(rew_cov, .95), max(rew_cov)),
               sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(all_ek %in% orig_keys)))),
  row.names = FALSE, caption = "(A2) Coverage of the 54 couplings of the three events: chance baselines.")

## (B) conclusion stability on original vs augmented network
check <- function(g) {
  E_all <- ecount(simplify(g, remove.multiple = TRUE, remove.loops = FALSE))  # edge count incl. the PP self-loop
  g <- simplify(g, remove.multiple = TRUE, remove.loops = TRUE)
  nm <- V(g)$name; ind <- degree(g, mode = "in"); outd <- degree(g, mode = "out"); lv <- layer_fine[nm]
  net <- sapply(L4, function(k) sum(outd[lv == k]) - sum(ind[lv == k]))
  list(N = vcount(g), E = E_all, src = sort(nm[ind == 0]),
       to = nm[which.max(outd)], tov = max(outd), ti = nm[which.max(ind)], tiv = max(ind),
       nfi = ind[nm == "NF"], nfo = outd[nm == "NF"], net = net,
       C1 = setequal(nm[ind == 0], c("SEQ", "EQ")),
       C2 = (nm[which.max(outd)] == "SEQ" && nm[which.max(ind)] == "CF"),
       C3 = (ind[nm == "NF"] > outd[nm == "NF"]),
       C4 = (net[["Trigger"]] > net[["Natural"]] && net[["Natural"]] > net[["Engineering"]] &&
             net[["Engineering"]] > net[["Consequence"]] && net[["Trigger"]] > 0 && net[["Consequence"]] < 0))
}
g_aug <- graph_from_data_frame(unique(rbind(E_orig, E_extra)), directed = TRUE)
b0 <- check(g_marine); b1 <- check(g_aug)
fmt <- function(b) c(sprintf("%d / %d", b$N, b$E), paste(b$src, collapse = ", "),
  sprintf("%s (%d)", b$to, b$tov), sprintf("%s (%d)", b$ti, b$tiv), sprintf("%d / %d", b$nfi, b$nfo),
  sprintf("%+d / %+d / %+d / %+d", b$net[["Trigger"]], b$net[["Natural"]], b$net[["Engineering"]], b$net[["Consequence"]]),
  b$C1, b$C2, b$C3, b$C4)
tabB <- data.frame(Quantity = c("Nodes / edges", "Pure sources", "Top out-degree", "Top in-degree",
  "NF in / out", "Layer net flow T/N/E/C", "C1 sources are only SEQ,EQ",
  "C2 SEQ out-hub & CF in-hub", "C3 NF is convergence node", "C4 monotone four-layer cascade"),
  `Original (58 events)` = fmt(b0), `Augmented (61 events)` = fmt(b1), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(tabB, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "(B) Core conclusions before and after merging the three independent events.")

## (C) node-importance rank stability (Spearman)
cm <- intersect(V(g_marine)$name, V(g_aug)$name)
so <- cor(degree(g_marine, mode = "out")[cm], degree(g_aug, mode = "out")[cm], method = "spearman")
si <- cor(degree(g_marine, mode = "in")[cm],  degree(g_aug, mode = "in")[cm],  method = "spearman")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Metric = c("Out-degree ranking", "In-degree ranking"),
  `Spearman (orig vs augmented)` = sprintf("%.3f", c(so, si)), check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE, caption = "(C) Node-importance rank stability under the new data.")
```

# Discussion: supporting numbers {#discussion-checks}

**What it shows / why:** three further numbers quoted in the Discussion. (1) How far
the submarine earthquake reaches: the hazards it triggers directly and those it reaches
within two steps. (2) Documentation depth: the marine events that document no
consequence-layer hazard, and those whose chains stop at the natural-process layer.
(3) An equal-sample check of the marine–inland contrast: 1000 random draws of 58 of
the 84 inland events, each rebuilt as a 15-class network and compared with the marine
network on density, out- and in-degree centralisation and consequence-layer net flow.

```{r discussion-checks}
## (1) reach of the submarine earthquake in the fine network
dc_d <- distances(g_marine, v = "SEQ", mode = "out")[1, ]
dc_d <- dc_d[names(dc_d) != "SEQ"]
cat(sprintf("SEQ triggers %d of the other %d hazards directly and reaches %d within two steps\n",
            sum(dc_d == 1), length(dc_d), sum(dc_d <= 2)))

## (2) documentation depth: the layers that the chains of each marine event reach
dc_layers <- lapply(rc_evs, function(e) unique(layer_fine[c(rc_pairs(rc_enc[rc_has & rc_ev == e]))]))
stopifnot(!anyNA(unlist(dc_layers)))
dc_nocons <- !vapply(dc_layers, function(l) "Consequence" %in% l, logical(1))
dc_natend <- !vapply(dc_layers, function(l) any(c("Engineering", "Consequence") %in% l), logical(1))
cat(sprintf("marine events with no consequence-layer hazard: %d of %d; of these, stopping at the natural-process layer: %d\n",
            sum(dc_nocons), length(rc_evs), sum(dc_natend)))

## (3) equal-sample check: 1000 draws of 58 of the 84 inland events. Each event's
## couplings are parsed once; a draw is the union of its events' couplings, simplified
## (duplicate edges and self-loops removed) exactly as for Table 3.
dc_in_enc <- encoding_of(xin)
dc_in_key <- lapply(rc_in_evs, function(e) {
  p <- rc_pairs(dc_in_enc[has_chain & ev_in == e]); unique(paste(p[, 1], p[, 2], sep = "|")) })
dc_inland <- function(idx) {
  k <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(unique(unlist(dc_in_key[idx])), "|", fixed = TRUE))
  simplify(graph_from_data_frame(data.frame(from = k[, 1], to = k[, 2]), directed = TRUE),
           remove.multiple = TRUE, remove.loops = TRUE)
}
stopifnot(setequal(ekey(dc_inland(seq_along(rc_in_evs))), ekey(g_inland_c)))   # all 84 = the Table 3 network
dc_metrics <- function(g) c(edge_density(g, loops = FALSE), Cfree(g, "out"), Cfree(g, "in"),
                            layer_flow(g, layer15, L4)$`Net %`[4])
dc_marine <- dc_metrics(g_marine_c)
dc_inl84  <- dc_metrics(g_inland_c)
set.seed(1)
dc_draws  <- t(replicate(1000, dc_metrics(dc_inland(sample(length(rc_in_evs), 58)))))
dc_fmt    <- c("%.3f", "%.3f", "%.3f", "%+.1f%%")
dc_dir    <- c(-1, 1, 1, -1)   # inland: lower density, higher centralisation, more negative consequence flow
dc_share  <- vapply(1:4, function(j) 100 * mean(dc_dir[j] * (dc_draws[, j] - dc_marine[j]) > 0), numeric(1))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Metric = c("Network density (inland lower)", "Out-degree centralisation (inland higher)",
             "In-degree centralisation (inland higher)", "Net flow — Consequence (inland more negative)"),
  Marine                         = vapply(1:4, function(j) sprintf(dc_fmt[j], dc_marine[j]), ""),
  `Inland, 84 events`            = vapply(1:4, function(j) sprintf(dc_fmt[j], dc_inl84[j]), ""),
  `Inland, 58-event draws (range)` = vapply(1:4, function(j)
                                     paste(sprintf(dc_fmt[j], range(dc_draws[, j])), collapse = " to "), ""),
  `Draws in that direction`      = sprintf("%.0f%%", dc_share), check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Equal-sample check of the marine–inland contrast: 1000 random draws of 58 of the 84 inland events.")
```

# Interactive viewer data {#viewer-data}

**What it makes / why:** the interactive network viewer linked from the figure
captions (`docs/index.html`, served at
<https://hazardchain.github.io/marine-seismic-hazard-chains-code-data/>) is driven
by `docs/graph-data.js`. This chunk regenerates that file **from the very same
graph objects** used for the tables and figures above (`g_marine`,
`g_marine_c`, `g_inland_c`), so the web page, the paper figures, and the
tables are guaranteed to be one and the same network — no hand-maintained copy
can drift. `jsonlite` ships with `rmarkdown`, so knitting this document already
provides it. The only extra input is the human-readable peril names used for
the tooltips.

```{r viewer-data}
## full peril names for the 39 fine nodes (viewer tooltips only; no metric uses them)
full_name_fine <- c(
  SEQ="Submarine Earthquake", EQ="Coastal Earthquake", AS="Aftershock", VE="Volcanic Eruption",
  SLS="Submarine Landslide", CLS="Coastal Landslide", LS="Landslide", RO="Rockfall", LB="Lake Burst",
  SA="Snow Avalanche", LI="Liquefaction", GU="Ground Uplift", SUB="Subsidence", MB="Methane Blowout",
  TS="Tsunami", CFL="Coastal Flooding", FF="Fluvial Flood", MED="Marine Ecosystem Damage",
  WP="Water Pollution", WD="Water Dilemma", DI="Disease", FA="Flora and Fauna",
  PHF="Port / Harbour Failure", SDF="Seawall / Dike Failure", SPF="Subsea Pipeline Failure",
  SCF="Subsea Cable Failure", NFA="Nuclear Facility Accident", FI="Fire", EX="Explosion",
  CF="Critical Infrastructure Failure", NF="Critical Network Failure",
  MTD="Maritime Transport Disruption", BI="Business Interruption", EC="Economic Crisis",
  PP="Physical & Psychological Trauma", HD="Healthcare Degradation", IR="Insufficient Rescue",
  SU="Social Unrest", CP="Culture Perils")
stopifnot(setequal(names(full_name_fine), V(g_marine)$name))  # every fine node has a name

ident <- function(g) { n <- V(g)$name; setNames(n, n) }
mk_nodes <- function(g, label, full, layer) {
  nm <- V(g)$name
  df <- data.frame(id = nm, label = unname(label[nm]), full = unname(full[nm]),
                   layer = unname(layer[nm]),
                   `in`  = as.integer(degree(g, mode = "in")),
                   out   = as.integer(degree(g, mode = "out")),
                   check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df[order(df$id), , drop = FALSE]                 # deterministic order (platform-independent)
}
mk_edges <- function(g) { e <- igraph::as_data_frame(g)[, c("from", "to")]
  e[order(e$from, e$to), , drop = FALSE] }

## overlay: union of the original network and the three independent events;
## per-node "isNew" flag (touched by a new event) and per-edge category
## (novel = in the new events only; new = in both; old = original only).
mk_nodes_overlay <- function(g) {
  nm <- V(g)$name
  data.frame(id = nm, label = nm, full = unname(full_name_fine[nm]),
             layer = unname(layer_fine[nm]),
             `in`  = as.integer(degree(g, mode = "in")),
             out   = as.integer(degree(g, mode = "out")),
             isNew = nm %in% new_nodes,
             check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[order(nm), , drop = FALSE]
}
mk_edges_overlay <- function(g) {
  e <- igraph::as_data_frame(g)[, c("from", "to")]
  k <- paste(e$from, e$to); isN <- k %in% new_ekey; isO <- k %in% old_ekey
  e$cat <- ifelse(isN & !isO, "novel", ifelse(isN & isO, "new", "old"))
  e[order(e$from, e$to), , drop = FALSE]
}

GRAPHS <- list(
  fig1       = list(nodes = mk_nodes(g_marine,     ident(g_marine),     full_name_fine,     layer_fine),
                    edges = mk_edges(g_marine)),
  marine15   = list(nodes = mk_nodes(g_marine_c,   abbr, ident(g_marine_c),   layer15),
                    edges = mk_edges(g_marine_c)),
  inland15   = list(nodes = mk_nodes(g_inland_c,   abbr, ident(g_inland_c),   layer15),
                    edges = mk_edges(g_inland_c)),
  overlay    = list(nodes = mk_nodes_overlay(g_union), edges = mk_edges_overlay(g_union)))

if (!requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  message("jsonlite not available; skipping docs/graph-data.js regeneration.")
} else if (dir.exists("docs")) {
  js <- paste0(
    "// Auto-generated by marine_hazard_chains_reproduction.Rmd from the docx sources in data/. Do not edit by hand.\n",
    "const GRAPHS = ", jsonlite::toJSON(GRAPHS, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE), ";\n")
  writeLines(js, file.path("docs", "graph-data.js"))
  cat(sprintf("Wrote docs/graph-data.js  |  fig1 %d/%d, marine15 %d/%d, inland15 %d/%d, overlay %d/%d (nodes/edges)\n",
    nrow(GRAPHS$fig1$nodes),       nrow(GRAPHS$fig1$edges),
    nrow(GRAPHS$marine15$nodes),   nrow(GRAPHS$marine15$edges),
    nrow(GRAPHS$inland15$nodes),   nrow(GRAPHS$inland15$edges),
    nrow(GRAPHS$overlay$nodes),    nrow(GRAPHS$overlay$edges)))
} else {
  message("docs/ folder not found next to marine_hazard_chains_reproduction.Rmd; skipping viewer regeneration.")
}
```

The web viewer therefore shares its single source of truth with Figs 1–2 and
Tables 1–3: re-knit this document and the interactive page updates automatically.
